config.title: useMediaQuery

intro.title: useMediaQuery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that changes its appearance based on the user's screen size. You will learn how to use the `useMediaQuery` hook to detect and respond to CSS media queries directly in your TypeScript code. This involves working with React hooks, TypeScript types, and conditional rendering. By the end, you'll be able to create responsive UI elements that adapt to different devices like phones or desktops.
intro.usecase: The useMediaQuery hook is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen sizes in real-world applications. Developers use it to conditionally render components like navigation menus that switch between hamburger menus on mobile and full menus on desktop. It's commonly implemented in dashboards to rearrange data visualizations, in e-commerce sites to adjust product grid layouts, and in forms to optimize input field arrangements based on available space. This pattern ensures optimal user experience across devices without requiring separate codebases for different screen sizes.

objectives: Import the useMediaQuery hook from the @mui/material package into a React TypeScript component.
Define a media query string to target specific viewport breakpoints.
Invoke the useMediaQuery hook with a media query string to evaluate viewport conditions.
Store the boolean result from useMediaQuery in a component state variable.
Apply conditional rendering to display different UI elements based on the media query result.
Utilize TypeScript type annotations to ensure proper typing of the media query result.
Construct responsive UI components that adapt to different screen sizes.
Execute the useMediaQuery hook within a functional component to access viewport information.
Implement dynamic styling by applying CSS classes conditionally based on media query matches.
Control component behavior by using media query results in useEffect dependencies.
Return appropriate JSX structures that respond to changes in viewport dimensions.
Modify component layout and content organization in response to breakpoint changes.

steps.title: Initialize a state variable for screen width
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to declare a boolean state variable named isLargeScreen, initialized to false.
steps.hint: Remember to use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [isLargeScreen, setIsLargeScreen] = useState<boolean>(false);

// Example of declaring a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a boolean state variable called isLargeScreen that will track whether the screen is at a large width threshold.

isLargeScreen
boolean
false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isLargeScreen state variable. This will help us track whether the screen width meets our threshold.

steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the App component, use useState to create a boolean state variable called isLargeScreen with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Define the media query string
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a constant variable named 'mediaQuery' with the string value '(min-width: 768px)'.
steps.hint: Add a const declaration inside the component body, before the return statement. The value should be a string representing a CSS media query.
steps.analogousExample:
// Define a media query string
const mediaQuery = '(min-width: 768px)';
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a constant variable named 'mediaQuery' with the value '(min-width: 768px)' defined inside your App component.
successCriteria: The code must include a constant declaration named 'mediaQuery' with the exact string value '(min-width: 768px)' inside the App component body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the media query string that will be used to detect screen size changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a constant named 'mediaQuery' with the exact string value '(min-width: 768px)' inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query string wasn't defined correctly. You need to create a constant variable named 'mediaQuery' with the value '(min-width: 768px)' inside the App component.

steps.title: Call useMediaQuery with the query string
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, call the useMediaQuery hook with the mediaQuery string you defined earlier. Store the boolean result in a variable (e.g., matches).
steps.hint: The useMediaQuery hook takes a media query string as its argument and returns a boolean indicating whether the query matches.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of calling useMediaQuery with a query string
const matches = useMediaQuery('(min-width: 768px)');
steps.expectedOutcome: The useMediaQuery hook is called with the mediaQuery string, and its boolean result is stored in a variable.
successCriteria: useMediaQuery is called with mediaQuery as argument
The result is stored in a variable (e.g., matches)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the useMediaQuery hook with your media query string and stored the boolean result. This will tell you whether the screen matches your defined condition.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling useMediaQuery with the mediaQuery variable and storing the result in a variable. The hook should be called directly with the query string as its argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on just calling the useMediaQuery hook. Inside your component, call useMediaQuery(mediaQuery) and store the result in a variable like 'matches'.

steps.title: Add a heading to display the screen status

You'll need to use the result from useMediaQuery (which you haven't stored yet) - for now, create a variable called 'isLargeScreen' to store the useMediaQuery result, then use it in a conditional expression.
steps.hint: First call useMediaQuery and store the result in a variable. Then use that variable in a ternary operator inside the h2 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a heading that displays 'Large screen' or 'Small screen' based on the media query result.
